summary: Simulated three-judge panel (AI opinion; Wharton publishes no weights or scores). Scoring what exists today (11 filled WInS notes, no reflections yet; IPS V5, which the team calls AI-generated; a 10-line Final Report journal): Investment Strategy 6, Client Knowledge 5, Portfolio Analysis 4, Articulation 2, Creativity and Presentation 4. Average 4.2, against an estimated Top-50 bar of about 8+ on all five ('score exceptionally well on all five components', faqs.txt:79). On today's path the entry would rank roughly 350-700 of ~2,300 (low confidence). The strategy idea is top-decile; the losses are on the criteria students must earn themselves: an authentic voice, a true experience story, and projections they own. New findings: (1) the 16 Oct model makes the co-sponsor range more certain (99.4%) than the payments (about 6-7% of paths leave a later payment short of what Laura kept), which inverts the case's priority (case:91, 119-120), yet V5 says 'cannot miss'; (2) 'appropriate diversification' is a named criterion, but 'diversif-' appears 0 times in V5, a regression from V3, and [AI] suggestion 8 would delete the last defence; (3) [AI] suggestions 8, 9 and 13 cut scored content (diversification, the review rule, a cushion job) and 5 adds a wrong-basis cost, all to make room for a range and confidence the IPS is 'not expected' to include; (4) the team's most original, sourced insight (funders count only committed money; announced lead gifts raise others' giving) is unused, while the pitch opens with a claim that has no source in the repo; (5) in the median case Laura gives about 86% of the money not reserved, and at p5 she keeps $0, which tests 'responsibly' and flexibility (case:102-103). Ladder conflict re-run and reproduced: $294,461 (ideal ladder priced to 1 Jan payment dates, forward) vs $298,628 (Caplet's holdings' maturities, curve unchanged; $297,847 forward). A third figure, $295,924 (par yields used as zero rates), also sits in results.json. Use the holdings basis (~$298k, room ~$1.4k-$2.2k, 5-7bp, 15 Oct) for any claim about Caplet's plan or WInS book. Best points per hour before the IPS: reject the harmful [AI] suggestions; add a diversification principle; set an honest certainty standard; name liquidity, flexibility and uncertainty and a return assumption; one name per idea; a pitch built on the cap rule. These take about 5.5 hours for about +6 points. A fresh student IPS and student-written reflections are low-ratio gates that cannot be skipped.

findings.title: The plan's own model makes the co-sponsor range more certain than the payments, inverting the case's priority
findings.problem: The case puts the ten payments first ('high degree of certainty') and says the range must also protect them. The 16 Oct model shows the gift inside the range in 99.4% of paths, while in about 6-7% of paths a later payment needs more than Laura kept. The floor is paid out in 2033, before most of the reinvestment shortfall appears. V5 claims 'cannot miss the range', and [AI] suggestion 12 would print '99 times in 100' for the range. A bond judge will ask why the promise to co-sponsors is safer than the promise to the artists.
evidence: Laura_Gao_2026_Client_Profile.txt:91 'must be funded by the investment portfolio with a high degree of certainty'
Laura_Gao_2026_Client_Profile.txt:119-120 'The proposed range must also protect the portfolio's ability to fund the ten-year operating commitment.'
findings.fix: Team picks one of the number sheet's options (state the risk; keep Laura's half to 2042; hold a buffer from the 2028 deposit) so that payment certainty is at least as high as range certainty, and writes it as a principle in the IPS. No range-confidence figure is quoted without the payment figure beside it.

findings.title: 'Appropriate diversification' is a criterion; V5 never argues it and [AI] suggestion 8 deletes the last defence

findings.title: V5 names only 3 of the Guide's 6 IPS themes and states no return assumption

V5 never uses 'liquidity', 'flexibility' or 'uncertainty'. The IPS brief asks for the approach to 'risk and return', and the case lists 'return expectations', but V5 uses 'return' only as a verb. The missing uncertainty and return are new; liquidity and flexibility were flagged before.

findings.fix: Each of the six themes is visibly handled as a principle. One return assumption is stated. Liquidity is covered, including where money waits between a bond's maturity and the 1 January payment. Students' words.

findings.title: Pitch spends its hook on an unsupported claim and a stale number and omits the original cap rule
findings.problem: The pitch is the first thing a screening reader sees. It opens with 'co-sponsors who fund the building rarely pay to run it', which has no source anywhere in the repo; the case says outside sources 'may' fund operations. It quotes '$292,000', which is wrong on every basis now. It never mentions the cap rule (gift = floor + half the fund, never above the announced top), which is the plan's most original idea and its answer to the case's credibility concern.
evidence: repo-wide grep 16 Oct for 'rarely pay'/'pay to run': only V4 notes and V5
findings.fix: The pitch states Laura's goal and the central idea, including the cap mechanism. No figure that can go stale, no unsupported claim, 45 words or fewer. Written by students.

findings.title: Ladder cost: three figures in circulation; only the holdings basis fits Caplet's claims
findings.problem: Reproduced on the 15 Oct curve: payment dates $294,461 (19.0bp room) forward / $295,246 unchanged; Caplet's holdings' maturities $297,847 (7.4bp) forward / $298,628 (4.7bp) unchanged. About $3.4k of the gap comes from bonds maturing 0.5-10.5 months before each payment; about $0.8k from the curve basis. results.json also stores $295,924 / $4,076 (13.4bp) with 'par yields used as zero rates'. The sheet's 35% over-$300k chance is anchored to $294,453; on the holdings basis it is about 44-45% (sibling MODEL). [AI] suggestion 5 would put $294,000 into the IPS.
findings.fix: For any claim about Caplet's plan or WInS book, use one dated holdings-basis figure (about $298k, room $1.4k-$2.2k, 5-7bp on 15 Oct), the same way in all three documents. Or put no figure in the IPS and the figure in the Final Report with its date and basis. A student re-runs it and can explain the date gap.
